title: Me siento mal
subtitle: Four scenes about small health problems
register: casual (tú), a couple at home, Mexican Spanish
review: Written by Claude in Latin American (Mexican) Spanish. Check the Spanish, the English lines, the notes and the questions.
intro: A cold, a phone call nobody should make, a pot of chicken broth that is always full and a cure that works on everything: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas, and Lucas's mother. Listen for me duele, for tengo with what you have, and for how you say you feel better.

lines.note: Sentirse bien / mal: to feel well / sick. Me siento mal.
Word for word: what do you have? The usual question to someone who looks sick.

lines.text: Me duele la garganta. Tengo tos. Y me escurre la nariz.

tr.en: My throat hurts. I have a cough. And my nose is running.

lines.note: Me duele + the part of the body. Tener tos: to have a cough. Me escurre la nariz is Mexican; elsewhere, me gotea la nariz.
In Mexico la gripa is the everyday word for a cold. Elsewhere: un resfriado, la gripe.

lines.text: Creo que es algo más grave.

tr.en: I think it's something more serious.

lines.note: Grave: serious. Algo más grave: something more serious.
Tener fiebre, with no article.
How a temperature is said aloud: 37.2 = treinta y siete dos. Normal is about 37.

lines.text: Voy a llamar a mi mamá.

tr.en: I'm going to call my mom.

lines.note: Ir a + infinitive: going to. Llamar a + the person.

lines.text: Porque en veinte minutos está aquí con una olla de caldo de pollo.

tr.en: Because in twenty minutes she'll be here with a pot of chicken broth.

lines.note: Una olla: a big pot. Caldo de pollo: chicken broth, the family cure for everything. The present, está, for something that is sure to happen.
Me duele la cabeza = tengo dolor de cabeza.
Desde que + verb: since something happened. Llegó: she arrived.

lines.text: Dice que es porque andas descalza.

tr.en: She says it's because you go around barefoot.

lines.note: Andar descalzo: to go barefoot. The classic explanation for any illness. Descalza, because it is about Emma.

lines.text: Me duele la cabeza, no los pies.

tr.en: It's my head that hurts, not my feet.

lines.note: Two feet, so it would be me duelen los pies.

lines.text: Dice que todo empieza por los pies.

tr.en: She says everything starts with the feet.

lines.note: Empezar por: to start with.
A menthol ointment found in every Mexican home, and its answer to every illness.
En todos lados = en todas partes.
¡Ay! is what you say when it hurts.
Pasar: to happen. ¿Qué pasó? is also a Mexican hello.
Levantar: to lift. Pesado: heavy.
A common way to ask what exactly.

lines.text: La olla de caldo de mi mamá.

lines.note: Lleno, llena: full. Estaba: was.

tr.en: You should go to the doctor.

lines.note: Deberías + infinitive: you should. In Mexico people say el doctor more than el médico.

lines.text: Mi mamá dice que no hace falta.

tr.en: My mom says there's no need.

lines.note: No hace falta: it isn't necessary.
The rhyme every mother says to a child who is hurt. It goes on: si no sanas hoy, sanarás mañana.
Funcionar: to work.

lines.text: No. Pero ya me puso vaporub.

tr.en: No. But she's already put vaporub on me.

lines.note: Poner: to put on. Me puso: she put on me. Ya: already.

lines.text: Un poco mejor. Pero todavía estoy débil.

tr.en: A little better. But I'm still weak.

lines.note: Mejor: better. Todavía: still. Débil: weak.
Tomar or tomarse la medicina: to take medicine.

lines.text: Dos veces al día, después de comer.
lines.note: Una vez, dos veces, tres veces al día.

tr.en: Good. Can you wash the dishes?

lines.note: Lavar los platos: to do the dishes.
Estar mareado: to feel dizzy.

lines.text: Qué lástima. Tu mamá quiere quedarse otra semana para cuidarte.

tr.en: What a shame. Your mom wants to stay another week to take care of you.

lines.note: Quedarse: to stay. Cuidar: to take care of. Otra semana, without una.

lines.text: Es un milagro. Ya me siento muy bien.

tr.en: It's a miracle. I feel fine now.

lines.note: Ya: now, already. Me siento muy bien.

lines.text: Qué bueno. Los platos están en la cocina.

tr.en: Glad to hear it. The dishes are in the kitchen.

lines.note: Qué bueno: that's good, I'm glad.

notes: Pain: me duele + one thing, me duelen + more than one. Me duele la cabeza, la garganta, la espalda. Me duelen los pies.
What you have goes with tener: tengo tos, tengo fiebre, tengo gripa.
Feeling: me siento mal, me siento un poco mejor, ya me siento muy bien. Estoy mareado, estoy débil.
Advice: deberías + infinitive. Deberías ir al doctor.
Medicine: tomar la medicina, dos veces al día, después de comer.
Mexican words: la gripa (a cold), me escurre la nariz (my nose is running), el doctor, en todos lados.
Dice que…: he or she says that… Mi mamá dice que no hace falta.

questions.q: Why doesn't Emma want Lucas to call his mom?
options: She will arrive with a pot of chicken broth.
questions.why: En veinte minutos está aquí con una olla de caldo de pollo.

questions.q: According to Lucas's mom, why does Emma have a headache?
questions.why: Dice que es porque andas descalza. Todo empieza por los pies.

options: La olla de caldo de su mamá
questions.why: La olla de caldo de mi mamá. Siempre está llena.

questions.q: How often does Lucas take his medicine?
questions.why: Dos veces al día, después de comer.

questions.q: Why does Lucas suddenly feel fine?
options: His mom wants to stay another week.
questions.why: Tu mamá quiere quedarse otra semana para cuidarte. The miracle follows at once.
